episodes.title: Pilot
probes: Walt spends the morning of his fiftieth birthday at the kitchen table with Skyler and their teenage son.
After teaching all day, Walt puts in hours at his second job at a car wash.
Walt tags along in the car while Hank and other DEA agents raid a meth lab.

episodes.title: Cat's in the Bag...
probes: At an ultrasound appointment, Skyler presses Walt about the late-night phone call she overheard the other night.

episodes.title: ...And the Bag's in the River
probes: Hank drives Walt Jr. out to a rundown motel to lecture him about gateway drugs.
Walt and Jesse spend the day cleaning up what is left of Emilio in the ruined bathroom.
Carrying food down to the basement, Walt collapses partway down the stairs.

episodes.title: Cancer Man
probes: Jesse turns up at his parents' immaculate suburban house, and they are dismayed at the state he's in.
Jesse's much younger brother is a star at both sports and music, under heavy pressure from their parents.
Jesse grows convinced law enforcement is closing in on him and becomes increasingly paranoid.

episodes.title: Gray Matter
probes: Walt and Skyler attend an extravagant birthday party thrown by a wealthy former colleague from Walt's graduate school days.
Caught by a cop trying to buy beer underage, Walt Jr. phones Hank instead of his own father.
Jesse keeps hitting walls trying to find steady, legitimate work outside the drug trade.

episodes.title: Crazy Handful of Nothin'
probes: Walt shaves his head after discovering his hair has started falling out.
Walt sits through his first chemotherapy session, hooked to the drip in the treatment room.
Their first batch of product brings in only $2,600, and Walt insists on ramping up production.

episodes.title: A No-Rough-Stuff-Type Deal
probes: Walt and Jesse can't get their hands on enough pseudoephedrine pills to keep production going.
Skyler hosts a baby shower at the house, unwrapping gifts in front of the assembled guests.
Walt and Jesse wrestle a large barrel of methylamine out of a locked warehouse at night.

episodes.title: Seven Thirty-Seven
probes: Hank sits going through security camera footage from the warehouse where the methylamine barrel went missing.

episodes.title: Grilled
probes: At the desert hideout Tuco cares for an elderly relative in a wheelchair who communicates only by ringing a bell.
Tuco talks up his idea of taking Walt south to Mexico to run a cooking operation in the jungle.
Hank, helping Skyler look for Walt, pays a visit to Jesse's mother at her home.

episodes.title: Bit by a Dead Bee
probes: Badger helps Jesse load all the lab equipment out of his house into the RV, which gets towed away.
Jesse holes up in a cheap motel room with a prostitute, telling anyone who asks he was there all weekend.
Walt and Jesse part ways in the desert and hitchhike separately back toward the city.

episodes.title: Down
probes: Walt takes Walt Jr. out for a driving lesson, trying to reconnect with his son.
With nowhere to sleep, Jesse climbs into the fenced lot where the RV sits and spends the night inside it.
Skyler starts disappearing for entire days, and refuses to tell Walt where she has been.
Jesse's motorbike is stolen, leaving him with nothing and nowhere to go.

episodes.title: Breakage
probes: Walt frets over a mounting pile of medical bills, including the charges from his hospital stay.
Jesse takes an interest in the young woman who lives next door and rents him his place.
Jesse, back on his feet, settles his debts and moves into a new apartment.

episodes.title: Peekaboo
probes: Jesse lets himself into a squalid house hunting the pair of addicts who ripped off Skinny Pete.
Walt is back at school, standing in front of his chemistry class again after his time away.
Jesse makes food for a filthy, neglected little boy in a wrecked house and sits watching TV with him.

episodes.title: Negro y Azul
probes: Unable to reach Jesse, Walt takes it upon himself to make the product deliveries to the street dealers.
Jesse holes up at home, ignoring calls, while Walt keeps trying to get hold of him.
Skyler goes job hunting and ends up back at the bookkeeping desk of her old employer.
Hank, transferred to the El Paso office, is the odd man out among agents who treat him as a gringo.

episodes.title: 4 Days Out
probes: Walt and Jesse haul supplies into the RV for a marathon cook stretched across a long weekend in the desert.
Walt and Jesse end up sitting outside the RV in the freezing desert with no food or water left.
Walt tells his family he is going away to visit his mother for a few days.
Jesse has left the RV's keys sitting in the ignition, and the battery is drained flat.

episodes.title: Over
probes: At a backyard party for family and friends, Walt keeps refilling Walt Jr.'s glass with tequila.
Skyler organizes a gathering to thank everyone who supported the family through Walt's illness.
Jesse is caught off guard when Jane's father drops by unannounced to see her.

episodes.title: Mandala
probes: Saul lays out an entirely new way of moving product now that street-level dealing has stopped working.

episodes.title: Phoenix
probes: Walt Jr. sits at a computer building a donations website asking strangers to help pay his father's medical bills.
Jesse comes demanding his share of the money, and Walt tells him he must first prove he's clean.

episodes.title: ABQ
probes: Walt Jr.'s donation website takes off, and local news crews take an interest in the family's story.
Walt lies on a hospital gurney, groggy and slurring as the anesthetic takes hold before his operation.
Walt drives through the roughest corners of Albuquerque at night, searching for Jesse.

episodes.title: No Más
probes: Jesse sits through sessions at a rehab facility, wrestling with self-loathing and guilt.
Walt rattles around the house alone, packing up his things while Skyler stays elsewhere with the kids.
The whole city is still reeling, in a daze over the mid-air collision in the skies above Albuquerque.
Two silent, identically dressed brothers make their way across the border from Mexico into the United States.

episodes.title: Caballo sin Nombre
probes: A patrol officer stops Walt over the crack running across his car's windshield, and the roadside exchange escalates.
Jesse wanders through his old house, freshly renovated and staged, with a for-sale sign out front.
Walt Jr. cannot understand why his mother still refuses to let his father come back home.

episodes.title: I.F.T.
probes: Jesse, still unable to shake Jane's death, has moved back into his old house alone.
Told he is being sent back to El Paso, Hank loses his temper in a bar.
Walt Jr. is delighted to have his father back in the house and baffled by his mother's coldness.

episodes.title: Green Light
probes: Walt barges into the office building where Skyler works, loudly demanding to see her boss.
Jesse turns up waiting for Walt outside the school, eager to show off a batch he cooked alone.

episodes.title: Más
probes: Marie, worried about how Hank is doing, confides in Skyler about it.
Hank keeps digging away at the RV lead, and it sparks an argument with Marie.
Gus tells Walt that a man provides for his family whether or not they appreciate him for it.

episodes.title: Sunset
probes: Walt Jr., in the wake of the divorce, presses for straight answers about his parents' relationship.
Walt takes a liking to the well-qualified new assistant brought in to help him in the lab.
Jesse brings Badger and Skinny Pete back in, recruiting them to work the drug trade alongside him again.

episodes.title: One Minute
probes: Hank sits with Marie and tearfully talks about how much his work has changed him since the desert shootout.
Walt goes out of his way to needle his fastidious lab assistant, making the superlab an unpleasant place to work.

episodes.title: I See You
probes: Left alone in the underground lab, Jesse can't get a cook started and frets about hitting their quota.

episodes.title: Kafkaesque
probes: The new lab is running at full tilt, with Walt and Jesse comfortably hitting two hundred pounds a week.

episodes.title: Fly
probes: A single housefly gets into the lab, and Walt goes to absurd lengths trying to swat it.
Walt lies awake with insomnia, brooding over the direction his life has taken.
Jesse, dismissive at first, ends up joining Walt's obsessive hunt around the lab equipment.
Jesse, learning Walt has not slept in two days, quietly slips sleeping pills into his coffee.

episodes.title: Abiquiu
probes: Gus invites Walt to his home for dinner, cooking for him and offering some fatherly advice.
Badger and Skinny Pete balk at Jesse's idea of selling to people from their rehab group.
Skyler opens the first of Hank's hospital bills and starts pressing Walt about where the money comes from.

episodes.title: Half Measures
probes: In his hospital room, Marie gives Hank a sponge bath and makes him a playful wager.
Hank's doctors have told him he can go home whenever he likes, but he stays in his bed.

episodes.title: Full Measure
probes: Gus, going over the numbers with a chemist, says his overhead means he cannot lose even a week's production.

episodes.title: Box Cutter
probes: Hank, stuck at home after his injury, snaps at Marie and buries himself in collecting and cataloging minerals.
A jumpy Saul has taken on a personal bodyguard who follows him around.
Skyler cannot reach Walt on the phone and fears something has happened to him.

episodes.title: Thirty-Eight Snub
probes: Andrea stops by Jesse's place, worried about him; he presses a thick stack of cash on her for Brock.
Hank does his physical therapy sessions at home, and Marie is finding his mood harder and harder to bear.
Jesse installs an elaborate new stereo system in his living room, and the party there simply never ends.

episodes.title: Open House
probes: Walt seethes at the new motion-detecting surveillance camera watching him from the ceiling of the lab.
Jesse's house party runs around the clock, and he flings piles of cash into the middle of the chaos.
Marie spends her afternoons drifting alone through strangers' real-estate open houses.

episodes.title: Bullet Points
probes: Skyler hands Walt a typed list of talking points and makes him rehearse his confession line by line.
Walt grumbles about the wording of a speech he is supposed to deliver spontaneously to Hank and Walt Jr.
Hank asks Walt to read aloud a passage about a chemical process from a handwritten lab notebook.

episodes.title: Shotgun
probes: Walt and Skyler sign the paperwork that officially makes them the owners of the car wash.
Jesse rides along with Mike all day, driving from stop to stop across New Mexico picking up money.
Walt, agitated and alone at the lab, demands to know from Mike where Jesse has been taken.

episodes.title: Cornered
probes: Walt hands cash to three workers at the industrial laundry, having them come downstairs and scrub the lab.
Worn down by his son's pleading for a new car, Walt buys him a Dodge Challenger.

episodes.title: Problem Dog
probes: Skyler sits with far more cash than she expected, unsure the car wash can plausibly account for it.
Hank has Walt Jr. drive him out to Los Pollos Hermanos for a meal.
Jesse turns up again at his twelve-step meeting and speaks in front of the group.

episodes.title: Hermanos
probes: Gus sits at the bedside of the old man in the nursing home, speaking quietly to him about his nephews.
Walt again presses Jesse to use the poison on Gus at the very first opportunity he gets.

episodes.title: Bug
probes: Skyler pulls open a hatch and climbs down into the crawl space beneath the house, where the cash is kept.
Sitting in on a tax audit, Skyler plays the giggling, hopeless bookkeeper who knows nothing about standard accounting practices.
Jesse is put to work scrubbing a warehouse and hauling every trace of product out of it.

episodes.title: Salud
probes: In the morning Walt apologises to his son for the drugged state he was in the night before.
Walt fails to show up for his son's birthday gathering at the house.
Walt Jr. lets himself into his father's apartment and finds him bloodied and slurring, then stays the night to look after him.

episodes.title: End Times
probes: Skyler, Walt Jr. and the baby move into Hank and Marie's house, with agents watching outside.
Walt sits alone in his shuttered, barricaded house, furniture pushed against the doors, waiting for someone to come.

episodes.title: Face Off
probes: Detectives press Jesse with questions in a hospital corridor until Saul turns up and shuts the interview down.

episodes.title: Live Free or Die
probes: A wrecking-yard truck fitted with an enormous electromagnet is driven up against the wall of a police evidence building.
A ragged, bearded man eats breakfast alone at a Denny's counter in Albuquerque on his birthday.
News coverage of the three deaths at the Casa Tranquila senior center plays while Walt tidies up loose ends.

episodes.title: Madrigal
probes: A little robot vacuum trundles around the floor of Jesse's place while he hunts through the room.
At the DEA, agents work through a stack of leads left over from the Fring case, hoping one pans out.
Walt and Jesse sit down with Mike, trying to talk him into partnering with them on a new operation.

episodes.title: Hazard Pay
probes: The operation sets up inside a house sealed beneath a fumigation tent, the team posing as exterminators.
Walt carries his boxes back into the house and settles in again, much to Skyler's dismay.
Walt, Mike and Jesse sit down with Saul to run through possible locations for a new cooking site.

episodes.title: Fifty-One
probes: Walt's fifty-first birthday is marked with a small, joyless dinner at home, nobody much in the mood.
Jesse walks the aisles of a warehouse stacked with methylamine barrels alongside a jittery Lydia.
Mike scoffs at Lydia's panic, convinced she is inventing an excuse to wriggle out of their arrangement.

episodes.title: Dead Freight
probes: Walt Jr. drives over to the house demanding answers about what is going on, and Walt sends him away.
Walt pays a visit to Hank's new office at the DEA, the two of them talking alone in there.

episodes.title: Buyout
probes: Jesse endures an excruciating dinner at Walt and Skyler's house, straining to make small talk over the meal.
Saul accompanies Mike to a face-to-face sit-down with the DEA agents who have been tailing him.
Walt invites Jesse over to the house and talks about the company he helped found years ago.

episodes.title: Say My Name
probes: Out in the desert, Walt, Jesse and Mike stand facing Declan and his men to haggle over terms.

episodes.title: Gliding Over All
probes: Walt visits Jesse's house, and the two end up reminiscing fondly about their early days cooking in the cramped RV.
Months pass in a montage of tented houses, cooks and deliveries as the operation hums along profitably.

episodes.title: Blood Money
probes: Lydia turns up unannounced at the car wash, nervously asking after Walt while Skyler watches from the counter.

episodes.title: Buried
probes: Jesse sits alone on a playground merry-go-round, turning slowly in circles and staring at nothing.
An elderly man shuffles along a residential street, gathering up the bundles of cash left scattered across lawns and driveways.

episodes.title: Confessions
probes: Walt and Skyler sit down across from Hank and Marie in a public restaurant to try and negotiate.
At the table, Skyler tells Hank flatly that Walt is no longer any part of his empire.
Jesse sits saying nothing across from Hank in an interview room until Saul turns up.

episodes.title: Rabid Dog
probes: Walt comes home to find Saul's car crashed at an angle in his driveway and nobody inside.
Marie sits with her therapist, circling around her brother-in-law without saying everything she knows about him.
Walt leaves a message on Jesse's voicemail, asking him to meet so he can explain himself.
Walt spins his family a story about a malfunctioning pump at the gas station soaking him in gasoline.

episodes.title: Granite State
probes: A ragged Walt sits alone at a small-town bar with a television interview playing above the counter.
There is a pay phone in the bar, and Walt stands at it with the receiver in hand.
